MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR REFERRAL TO AN
EARLY SETTLEMENT CONFERENCE

I. AUTHORITY
Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(a)(5) identifies facilitating settlement as a purpose of a pretrial

conference. Rule 16(c)(2)(I) authorizes consideration of settlement and authorized procedures for
resolving the dispute. Local Civil Rule 83.6(A) permits litigants to request mediation and
authorizes settlement conferences; subsection (C) authorizes judicial officers to serve as mediators;
and subsection (G) authorizes court-directed attendance by counsel and/or representatives with
full settlement authority at an appropriate time.

I. REFERRAL IS APPROPRIATE NOW

Given the number and scope of the pending proceedings, an early settlement conference

may permit the parties to explore resolution before further judicial resources are committed.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document134 Filed 11/02/26 Page 2 of 4 PagelD#

Plaintiff requests an opportunity for court-assisted discussions and is willing to participate. The
designated magistrate judge can determine the arrangements necessary to conduct the conference.
The requested referral would leave the pending proceedings and existing deadlines
unchanged. Local Civil Rule 83.6(D) provides that appointment of a mediator does not itself
postpone or stay the case or extend existing deadlines. Plaintiff requests referral on that basis.
Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court refer this action to an early settlement

conference before a United States magistrate judge designated by the Court.

Date: November 3, 2026 Respectfully submitted,

—*D
